newsitem.title: USA: US Midwest direct hogs steady-up $0.50 - dealers.
newsitem.headline: US Midwest direct hogs steady-up $0.50 - dealers.

text.p: U.S. Midwest direct cash hog prices early Friday were steady to $0.50 per cwt higher, lifted by a strong tone to pork prices following nearly three weeks of reduced slaughter, livestock dealers said.
"Our margins are still in the red, but they're a little better," one packer buyer said.

Interior Iowa and southern Minnesota hogs sold steady at $56.00 to $57.00 in the country and $57.50 to $58.50 at plants. Illinois hogs sold steady to $0.50 higher at $56.50 to $57.50 in the country and $58.00 at plants. Indiana hogs were steady at $55.00-$55.50/country and $57.50-$58.00/plants.
Ohio hogs sold steady to $0.50 higher at $55.00, with a few at $56.00 in the country and $57.00 to $58.00 at plants.
Estimated pork cut-out values on Thursday rose $1.06 to $1.23 per cwt, USDA reported.

Fresh bone-in loins with 1/4-inch trim and weighing 13-18 lbs Thursday had a weighted average price of $155.00 per cwt, up $5.64 from Wednesday and up $15.00 from last Friday's close, USDA statistics showed.
The strong pork prices fueled ideas that packer demand could increase next week, several sources said.
